headline: Netanyahu issues 'Emergency!' appeal to right-wing voters
dek: VERIFIED FACT: CEC noon turnout 31.5%, up from 28.4% at noon in 2022 (+3.1 points), the highest at that hour since the 1973 election (Times of Israel, Ynetnews, Jerusalem Post, Al Jazeera liveblog agree on 31.5% and 1973). sources: Israel Central Elections Committee (CEC) noon figure, via Times of Israel / Ynetnews / Jerusalem Post / Al Jazeera liveblog
fault_line: Is record turnout a verdict on Netanyahu's war leadership, or a mobilisation race his 'Emergency!' post is trying to win in the final hours?

sections.what_happened: VERIFIED FACT: CEC noon turnout 31.5%, up from 28.4% at noon in 2022 (+3.1 points), the highest at that hour since the 1973 election (Times of Israel, Ynetnews, Jerusalem Post, Al Jazeera liveblog agree on 31.5% and 1973). COUNT DISCREPANCY, NOT HIDDEN: Ynet cites CEC director-general Dean Livne for 2,309,000 voters by midday; Israel National News / Jerusalem Post / Panorama round to 'nearly 2.4 million' / '2.39 million' -- ship the 31.5% figure and, if an absolute is needed, Ynet's 2,309,000 with Livne attribution. HEADLINE DISCREPANCY, NOT HIDDEN: Israel National News and LaPresse headlines say 'since 1977' while their own body text says 1973 -- ship 1973, never 1977. Netanyahu, after voting in West Jerusalem, posted 'Emergency!' on X, claiming left-wing activists were 'storming' polling stations while right-wing activists were 'indifferent', and warned of high Arab voter turnout; he also told reporters police arrested three people carrying money in bags in an alleged voter-bribe attempt (already recorded 1500-05). Polls close 22:00 Israel time; exit polls then; final results may slip to Thursday on special ballots (recorded 1400-04). MONITOR NOTE ONLY (single undeclared outlet, NOT asserted): Panorama (Albania) reports a man with a knife was arrested near opposition leader Yair Golan in Tel Aviv -- no second source retrieved.
sections.what_verified: CEC figure via Times of Israel (T3), Ynetnews (T3), Jerusalem Post (T3), Al Jazeera liveblog (T2, STATE (QA)) = 4 families, all agreeing on 31.5% and the 1973 comparison.
sections.what_disputed: Turnout says nothing about which bloc benefits: final polls put both major blocs below 61 seats (Channel 12 Midgam Oct 22-23: change bloc 56, governing coalition 50, Arab parties 14 -- recorded via EconoTimes in-window, poll not a count). Netanyahu's 'left storming / right indifferent' framing is a campaign claim, not a CEC breakdown; no bloc-by-bloc turnout split was retrieved. Arab-turnout readings conflict with the morning's ballot-shortage reports (Haaretz via TRT, 1500-05) -- both can be true (shortages in some Palestinian communities, high turnout overall), but neither proves the other's effect.
sections.why_matters: Record number, open verdict: 31.5% by noon, highest since 1973 -- and the incumbent's own 'Emergency!' post is the story inside the number. No result is claimed before the 22:00 Israel-time exit polls.
sections.context: Background: NEW IN-WINDOW -- Israel election: noon turnout 31.5%, highest at noon since 1973; Netanyahu issues 'Emergency!' appeal to right-wing voters

totw_analysis: Our read: Record number, open verdict: 31.5% by noon, highest since 1973 -- and the incumbent's own 'Emergency!' post is the story inside the number. No result is claimed before the 22:00 Israel-time exit polls. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Is record turnout a verdict on Netanyahu's war leadership, or a mobilisation race his 'Emergency!' post is trying to win in the final hours?
